debrief_questions: At what moment did the first officer's picture of occupancy change, and who else knew?
What information was the commit decision made on, and how old was it?
Who could name the incident commander at any given minute, and who could not?
What did the crowd change about the decision, and was that acknowledged out loud?
What would have had to be true for the decision to go the other way?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: Incomplete information about occupancy, a short window in which the first decisions foreclose the later ones, and a crowd whose expectations are not the officer's risk frame.
scenario_frames.setting: a two-storey timber-framed dwelling in a residential street
scenario_frames.situation: Companies arrive to a working fire in an occupied dwelling. The first-arriving officer has a partial account from a neighbour about who lives there and no confirmation about who is out.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a tactical worksheet. No assignment, order of operations or entry decision is recorded here or implied by the questions.
scenario_frames.title: A house fire at three in the morning

debrief_questions: When did anybody on the incident learn that the system was impaired?
What in the pre-incident information would have carried that, and did it?
Which assumptions in the initial plan depended on a working system?
Who owns the impairment process in this jurisdiction, and is that a finding for them rather than for the crews?
What would make this discoverable on arrival next time?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: A protection assumption that the building normally carries has been removed, quietly, by a process that is nobody on the incident's fault.
scenario_frames.setting: a mid-rise commercial occupancy under partial renovation
scenario_frames.situation: A fire is reported in a building where the sprinkler system has been impaired for contractor work and the alarm panel has been in trouble for two days. The impairment paperwork exists somewhere.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a guide to suppression system operation or impairment procedure. Both belong to the code and to the building owner.
scenario_frames.title: A commercial building whose suppression system is out of service

debrief_questions: How long after arrival did anybody with structural expertise get a say, and how was it requested?
How was the disputed occupancy count handled - which number drove the plan, and was the uncertainty stated?
What was the mechanism for stopping work if the structure moved, and who was authorised to use it?
Which trades' knowledge would have changed the picture, and does the jurisdiction have a way to reach them at 2am?
Who was talking to the families, from what point, and with what information?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: A rescue problem that is simultaneously an engineering problem, where the expertise that could answer the engineering question is not on the first alarm and the people who might be alive are on a clock.
scenario_frames.setting: a building under renovation in a dense block
scenario_frames.situation: Part of a floor system has come down during occupied hours. The number of people inside is disputed between the contractor, the building manager and a bystander. Adjacent structures are of unknown stability.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a collapse rescue or shoring manual. Structural collapse technical rescue is a specialist discipline with its own standards and this pack states none of them.
scenario_frames.title: A partial structural collapse with people unaccounted for

debrief_questions: What was the first reliable statement about what had been struck, and where did it come from?
Who from the utility was on scene or on the phone, and how long did that take?
How was the perimeter decided, and what was it protecting against?
Was the digging crew treated as a hazard, a resource or both?
What does the locate-and-mark record say, and whose finding is that?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: The correct response differs completely depending on what was struck, and the people who know are the crew standing closest to it.
scenario_frames.setting: a street excavation beside an occupied building
scenario_frames.situation: A crew digging in the street has struck something. The dispatch information is contradictory about what was struck. People are standing near the excavation.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a utility emergency procedure. What to do about a struck gas, electrical or water asset belongs to the utility and the jurisdiction.
scenario_frames.title: An excavator strikes a buried utility

debrief_questions: How was unified command actually established with the facility, and when?
What product information was available, how was it obtained, and how confident was it?
What drove the protective action decision, and who made it?
How were the facility's own responders accounted for?
Which of the trade disciplines on site had information nobody asked for?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: Two command systems - the facility's and the jurisdiction's - meet at a fence, while a protective action decision for the public needs making on incomplete product information.
scenario_frames.setting: a fenced industrial site with process piping and storage
scenario_frames.situation: A release has occurred inside a facility fence line. Site personnel have begun their own response. The wind is carrying towards a residential area.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a hazardous materials response guide. Product identification, protective distances, decontamination and entry all belong to the regulation, the emergency response guidance and the agency procedure.
scenario_frames.title: A release at a process facility

debrief_questions: What stopped, or did not stop, the third worker?
At what point was it stated out loud that this was now a recovery risk rather than a rescue, and who was empowered to say that?
What did the site's own permit and rescue arrangements say, and did anybody read them?
Who held the "nobody enters" authority, and was that person physically at the opening?
How does this jurisdiction train the reflex, rather than the knowledge?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: The single most reliably fatal pattern in this domain is the would-be rescuer, and the pressure to become one is at its maximum in the first ninety seconds.
scenario_frames.setting: a municipal wastewater structure
scenario_frames.situation: A maintenance worker is unresponsive in a below-grade space. A second worker has already gone in after them and is now also unresponsive. A third is at the opening.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a permit-required confined space entry or rescue procedure. Entry, atmospheric monitoring and retrieval are regulated activities and nothing about them is stated here.
scenario_frames.title: A worker down in a below-grade space

debrief_questions: How was the tempo of the incident managed against the tempo the audience expected?
Who on scene actually understood the access system, and how were they found?
What was the plan if the weather closed before the primary method worked?
How was information given to the two workers, and by whom?
What did the building's own rescue plan say it would do?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: A slow problem that feels fast, where the technically correct answer takes longer than everybody watching believes it should.
scenario_frames.setting: a high-rise with a suspended platform
scenario_frames.situation: A suspended access platform has failed on one side, leaving two workers at height in harnesses. The building's roof rigging is reachable. Weather is deteriorating.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a rope rescue or fall protection procedure. Technical rescue at height has its own standards and this pack reproduces none of them.
scenario_frames.title: Workers stranded on a facade access system

debrief_questions: How was the triage between cars decided, and by whom?
What did building engineering know that the crew did not, and how was that surfaced?
How was information given to occupants who could not be reached quickly?
What is the jurisdiction's arrangement with lift contractors, and is that a finding?
Was the medical complaint reassessed while the mechanical problem was being worked?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: A low-acuity problem that becomes a high-acuity one in one car, with a finite crew and several simultaneous demands.
scenario_frames.setting: a high-rise office building on generator power
scenario_frames.situation: Multiple cars are stopped with occupants inside during a utility outage. One occupant is reporting a medical complaint. Building engineering staff are present but the lift contractor is an hour away.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a lift release procedure. Moving a lift car is the contractor's and the code's business.
scenario_frames.title: An entrapment in a tall building during a power event

debrief_questions: How and when was traction power status confirmed, and by whom, to whom?
What did the responders do in the interval before that confirmation?
How was self-evacuation handled - as a problem or as a fact?
Where did the transit organization sit in the command structure, and had that ever been exercised?
What happened to communications underground, and what was the fallback?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: Two organizations with complete and non-overlapping halves of the information, a communications environment that degrades underground, and self-evacuating passengers.
scenario_frames.setting: an underground station and the tunnel beyond it
scenario_frames.situation: A train has stopped between stations with passengers aboard and smoke reported. Traction power status is unclear to the responders and clear to the transit control centre, which is not on the responders' radio system.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a rail emergency procedure. Track access, power isolation and train evacuation belong to the transit authority and its regulator.
scenario_frames.title: A transit incident in a tunnel section

debrief_questions: How were arriving mutual aid units staged, and who told them?
Who held movement area authority and how did that interact with incident command?
What did the airfield emergency plan say, and when was it last walked with the mutual aid agencies?
How was the casualty count communicated, and to whom first?
What would have happened if the first unit had simply driven on?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: A controlled-access environment where the ordinary reflex - drive to the incident - is itself the hazard.
scenario_frames.setting: the movement area of a commercial airfield
scenario_frames.situation: An aircraft ground incident has occurred with the airfield still active. Mutual aid units are arriving at a perimeter gate and do not have movement area authorisation.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: an aircraft rescue and firefighting procedure. That discipline has its own standards, its own agents and its own training, none of which is here.
scenario_frames.title: A ground emergency at an airfield

debrief_questions: Who was in unified command, and how long did agreeing that take?
How was cargo information obtained and how confident was it?
What was the cost of stopping operations, and who was authorised to accept it?
How were terminal workers accounted for as distinct from ship's crew?
Which federal and state agencies had a role, and were they notified?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: Jurisdiction is genuinely unclear, cargo information is commercially held, and the terminal cannot simply be stopped without consequences that nobody on the first alarm is authorised to accept.
scenario_frames.setting: a container and bulk terminal on a working waterfront
scenario_frames.situation: An incident has occurred at a terminal with active cargo operations, a vessel alongside and a cargo manifest that is partly electronic and partly not.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a marine firefighting or port security procedure. Both are specialist, both are federally governed, and neither is described here.
scenario_frames.title: An incident at a working marine terminal

debrief_questions: Who made the evacuation decision and on what forecast product?
How was the uncertainty communicated to the public - was it communicated at all?
What was done for households without transport, and how were they identified before the day?
What did the previous unnecessary evacuation cost in credibility, and was that named in the decision?
Which institutions - care facilities, schools, custody - had a plan, and who checked?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: The decision has to be made while the evidence is still ambiguous, and the cost of being wrong is asymmetric in both directions.
scenario_frames.setting: a low-lying district behind flood defences
scenario_frames.situation: The forecast has moved. A decision about evacuating a district has to be made hours before the water arrives, on a forecast with a stated uncertainty, in a community with previous experience of an evacuation that turned out to be unnecessary.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a flood fight or swiftwater rescue procedure. Levee operations and water rescue are separate disciplines with their own authorities.
scenario_frames.title: A river forecast to crest above a levee

debrief_questions: When was the evacuation trigger set, and by whom - before the day or during it?
How was the single access road deconflicted between incoming apparatus and outgoing residents?
What was said to residents who intended to stay, and by whom?
How did the agencies with different legal authorities agree on one message?
Who was checking on the households that had been identified in advance, and had they been?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: Evacuation and suppression want the same road, the window is set by weather rather than by anybody's plan, and the decision authority is split across agencies.
scenario_frames.setting: a residential area at the edge of open land
scenario_frames.situation: A landscape fire is moving under wind towards a community on a single access road. Some residents are preparing to leave, some are preparing to stay, and the road is about to be needed in both directions.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a wildland fire tactics or evacuation procedure. Landscape fire behaviour and evacuation authority both belong elsewhere.
scenario_frames.title: A fire moving towards an interface community

debrief_questions: Who led the interaction, and was that agreed before the door or at it?
What was the slowest acceptable tempo, and did anybody protect it?
How was the family member's pressure handled without dismissing their information?
At what point would the legal authority to act have changed, and did everybody present know that line?
What happened after - who owned the follow-up, and was the loop closed?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: Three obligations in one doorway - safety, care and the person's own autonomy - with a family member applying pressure towards the fastest option.
scenario_frames.setting: a small flat with one person in acute distress
scenario_frames.situation: A call has come in from a family member. An officer and a crisis clinician arrive together. The person in distress is alone in a room and is not answering. The family member is asking the responders to do something now.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a crisis intervention protocol, a risk assessment instrument or a legal standard for involuntary intervention. All three belong to the state, the board and the behavioural health authority.
scenario_frames.title: A behavioural health call at a private address

debrief_questions: How long until one person could state the total casualty count, and how wrong was the first number?
What was done about casualties who arrived at hospitals by private car?
How was the boundary between the security problem and the medical problem managed in space and in command?
Which positional roles were filled late, and what did that cost?
Who was responsible for the uninjured thousands, and when did that start?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: Every service is at maximum, the structure has to be built while it is being used, and the informal system is outrunning the formal one.
scenario_frames.setting: an indoor venue with several thousand people present
scenario_frames.situation: A mass casualty incident has occurred at a public venue. The scene is not yet confirmed secure, casualties are being moved by members of the public, and hospitals are being self-referred to faster than they are being notified.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a triage system, a tactical response doctrine or a hospital surge plan. Each has an owner and none of them is this pack.
scenario_frames.title: A mass casualty event at a public venue

debrief_questions: On what day did this stop being a response problem, and who noticed?
Who was responsible for the medical needs of residents, as distinct from emergency response to them?
How was the voluntary agency's staffing limit surfaced, and by whom?
What was the exit plan for each resident, and when was it first written?
What did the conflict between residents reveal about the shelter's design rather than about the residents?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: The problem has silently changed category from response to social services, and the structure running it was designed for the first category.
scenario_frames.setting: a school gymnasium operating as a shelter
scenario_frames.situation: A shelter opened for an overnight event is still open on day four. The population has changed from evacuees to people with nowhere to go. Two residents are in conflict, one needs dialysis, and the voluntary agency staffing it is at the end of its rota.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a shelter operations manual or a medical special-needs sheltering standard. Both belong to the sheltering organizations and the state health authority.
scenario_frames.title: A congregate shelter on its fourth day

debrief_questions: What did the site's own emergency plan say, and had the fire service ever read it?
Who made the decision to hold rather than intervene, and on what basis?
How was the multi-hour nature of the incident resourced - relief, feeding, command continuity?
What was told to the neighbouring occupancies, and when?
Which trades on that site had the knowledge the incident needed?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: A hazard whose time constant is hours or days rather than minutes, in a facility whose operator has strong commercial reasons to minimise disruption.
scenario_frames.setting: a data centre campus with battery storage and on-site generation
scenario_frames.situation: A thermal event has been reported in a battery installation serving a data centre. Site staff have isolated what they believe they can. The behaviour of the installation over the next hours is not something anybody on scene has seen before.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a guide to energy storage system firefighting. That is an active, contested technical area owned by the codes and the manufacturers, and nothing about agents, isolation or entry is stated here.
scenario_frames.title: A thermal event in an energy storage installation

debrief_questions: Who first said the street itself was unsafe, and how long did that take?
How were cordons set with no engineering assessment available yet?
How were building inspectors and structural engineers requested, and how long did they take?
What was the message to a public that wanted to go back inside?
Which of the building trades could have answered the questions being asked, and is there a standing arrangement to reach them?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: The urge of every responder and every civilian is to be in the street, and the street is the hazard.
scenario_frames.setting: a downtown block of older masonry buildings
scenario_frames.situation: After a significant earthquake, the street is full of people, parapets and cladding are visibly displaced on several buildings, and the natural gathering point for the public is directly beneath them.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a post-earthquake safety evaluation procedure. Placarding and structural evaluation are the building official's and the engineer's.
scenario_frames.title: Facade and masonry hazard after an earthquake

debrief_questions: How was command shared with the operator's own rescue organisation?
What was the information route to the families, and who owned it from the first hour?
How was the temptation to commit untrained responders managed?
When did the statutory regulator arrive, and what changed then?
What was the plan for a multi-day operation, written on day one?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: Specialist capability sits with the operator, statutory authority sits with regulators who are not yet on scene, and the families are already at the gate.
scenario_frames.setting: a tunnel or mine working with a single access
scenario_frames.situation: Workers are unaccounted for beyond a blockage in an underground working. Atmosphere beyond the blockage is unknown. The operator has its own trained rescue capability and its own commercial exposure.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a mine or tunnel rescue procedure. Underground rescue is a regulated, certified discipline and nothing about it is described here.
scenario_frames.title: Entrapment in an underground works

debrief_questions: Who was authorised to permit re-entry, and did the crews on scene know that?
What was told to residents about the hazard, in what language, and in writing?
How were the responders' own exposures recorded?
Who picked up the residents' housing problem, and on what day?
Which remediation trades had to be involved, and did anybody have their number?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: The emergency is over and the hazard is not, which is exactly when the organisational attention leaves.
scenario_frames.setting: a fire-damaged mixed-use building of early twentieth century construction
scenario_frames.situation: The fire is out. Residents want their belongings. The building contains materials typical of its era, the water has been in it for twelve hours, and the owner wants a decision tonight.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: an asbestos, lead or mould assessment and abatement procedure. Each is a licensed activity governed by regulation.
scenario_frames.title: Re-entry to a fire-damaged older building

debrief_questions: How was the tension between rescue access and evidence preservation handled, and who arbitrated it?
Who assessed the stability of the remaining structure, and how long did that take?
How were site workers accounted for, given the site's own records?
When did the regulator and the investigating agency arrive, and what did they need that was already gone?
How was the wider construction workforce - who will all hear about this - supported?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: A rescue problem, a stability problem and a criminal-investigation problem occupying the same square metres from the first minute.
scenario_frames.setting: a downtown construction site with adjacent occupied buildings
scenario_frames.situation: A tower crane has failed, with debris across a street and into an adjacent building. The site was active. The failure mechanism is unknown and the remaining structure is still loaded.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a lifting equipment investigation or heavy rigging procedure. Failure analysis belongs to the regulator and to engineers.
scenario_frames.title: A crane failure in a city centre

debrief_questions: Who could actually describe the plant, and how were they found?
How was the pressure to keep the plant running handled, and by whom?
How were potentially exposed workers identified and accounted for, including those who had already gone home?
What information went to the receiving hospital, and when?
What does the facility's own emergency plan say, and had the fire service seen it?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: A commercial cost to the correct action, a symptomatic worker, and a plant that only three people in the building understand.
scenario_frames.setting: a cold storage warehouse with an industrial refrigeration plant
scenario_frames.situation: A refrigerant release has been reported in a plant room. Workers have self-evacuated, one is symptomatic, and the plant continues to run because stopping it has consequences for the stored product.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a refrigerant emergency procedure or an exposure treatment guide. The first belongs to the process safety regulation, the second to the medical director.
scenario_frames.title: A refrigerant release at a cold storage facility

debrief_questions: What did the permit system require, and what actually happened?
How did the fire get into the concealed space, and what does that say about the firestopping?
How was the investigation separated from the blame, in the first hour?
Who on the site knew the fire watch had ended, and who could have stopped the work?
Is this a finding for the crews, the contractor or the permit system?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: A preventable incident where the prevention system existed and did not run, and where the people who could say why are the people who will be blamed.
scenario_frames.setting: a partially occupied building undergoing fit-out
scenario_frames.situation: A fire has started in a concealed space during welding work on an occupied floor of a building under fit-out. The hot work permit system exists. The fire watch had ended.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a hot work permit procedure or a fire investigation methodology. Both have their own standards and their own qualified people.
scenario_frames.title: A fire started by hot work on an occupied site

debrief_questions: Who was the family's single point of contact, and how quickly was that named?
How was the workforce kept in service without pretending nothing had happened?
How were the investigation's needs and the agency's grief kept from colliding?
Who supported the supervisors, who were supporting everybody else?
What was in place before the day, and what had to be invented?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: Every organisational system is loaded at once, the people who would normally manage it are the people affected by it, and every decision is permanent in the family's memory.
scenario_frames.setting: an agency, its families and its community
scenario_frames.situation: A responder has been killed on duty. The agency has to continue responding, support a family, cooperate with an investigation, manage a public funeral and hold together a workforce that has just learned the job can do this.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a critical incident stress intervention, a line-of-duty death protocol or a benefits guide. The first is clinical, the second is the agency's and the association's, the third is statutory.
scenario_frames.title: The days after a line-of-duty death

debrief_questions: What did the jurisdiction independently know, and what did it take entirely on trust?
How was the protective action decision made and who signed it?
How was the message delivered to people who do not speak English and people without power?
When was this last exercised, and did the exercise allow failure?
What would the jurisdiction have done if the facility's information had been wrong?
scenario_frames.decision_pressure: The jurisdiction must make a public protective action decision using technical information it cannot independently verify, from an operator with its own interests, on a timeline set by the facility.
scenario_frames.setting: a jurisdiction inside a facility's emergency planning zone
scenario_frames.situation: A facility has made a notification that escalates its emergency classification. The jurisdiction's role is protective action for the public, and its information comes entirely from the facility.
scenario_frames.this_frame_is_not: a radiological emergency plan or a protective action guide. Both are federally governed and neither is stated here.
scenario_frames.title: An offsite notification from a major energy facility

em.name: Emergency Management and Disaster Relief

representation.endorsement_note: no organization named here has reviewed, approved or endorsed any part of this pack, and none has been contacted
kinds: public employee union representing county, state and municipal emergency management staff
coordinating network of voluntary and faith-based relief organizations
representation.what_they_do_here: a great deal of disaster relief is done by volunteers and non-governmental bodies who have no bargaining unit at all, and a training scaffold that only described government staff would be describing a minority of the people in the building

em.scope: preparedness, coordination, sheltering, resource movement and recovery - the work that happens above and around the incident rather than at it

tiers.name: Trained volunteer / community team member
tiers.what_the_role_is: a neighbour with training, working inside a structure, not an employee of anything

tiers.name: Emergency management specialist / planner
tiers.what_the_role_is: writes the plans, runs the exercises, maintains the relationships that have to exist before the day

tiers.name: Emergency management coordinator
tiers.what_the_role_is: runs a function or a facility during an activation and coordinates across agencies that do not report to them

tiers.name: Emergency management director
tiers.what_the_role_is: accountable to an elected official for the jurisdiction's preparedness and for what the activation does

tiers.name: ICS section-level role
tiers.what_the_role_is: a positional role inside an incident command structure - operations, planning, logistics, finance and administration - held for the duration and then handed back

tiers.name: ICS command-level role
tiers.what_the_role_is: incident commander or unified command member, including the information, safety and liaison roles that report to command

ems.name: Emergency Medical Services

representation.endorsement_note: no organization named here has reviewed, approved or endorsed any part of this pack, and none has been contacted
kinds: international labour union of fire fighters and fire-based emergency medical workers
public employee union representing third-service and county EMS staff
service employees union representing hospital-based and private-provider EMS staff
professional association of emergency medical technicians and paramedics
representation.what_they_do_here: who represents an EMS worker depends on who employs them, which is the single most confusing fact about this workforce and is recorded here rather than smoothed over

ems.scope: out-of-hospital emergency medical care and transport, delivered from fire departments, third services, hospital systems and private providers

tiers.name: Emergency medical responder level
tiers.what_the_role_is: the entry certification level; often held by people whose main job is something else entirely

tiers.name: Emergency medical technician level
tiers.what_the_role_is: the level most of the workforce holds, and the level most transport crews are built around

tiers.name: Advanced emergency medical technician level
tiers.what_the_role_is: an intermediate level that exists in some states and not others, which is itself worth a learner knowing

tiers.name: Paramedic level
tiers.what_the_role_is: the highest widely recognised out-of-hospital level, practising under a physician medical director's delegated authority

tiers.name: Field training officer / field supervisor
tiers.what_the_role_is: supervises crews in the field, signs off new members and is the first review of a difficult call

tiers.name: EMS officer / chief
tiers.what_the_role_is: runs the service: staffing, quality, medical direction relationship, and the answer when it goes wrong

fire.name: Fire Service

representation.endorsement_note: no organization named here has reviewed, approved or endorsed any part of this pack, and none has been contacted
kinds: international labour union of fire fighters and fire-based emergency medical workers
professional association of fire chiefs and fire officers
state and provincial associations of fire fighters
representation.what_they_do_here: they represent the workforce and the officers respectively; they are named as the kind of body a reader would go to, not as a party to this

fire.scope: fire suppression, rescue, hazardous materials response and, in most of the country, the first medical response as well

tiers.name: Recruit / probationary firefighter
tiers.what_the_role_is: in an academy or a probationary period, working under direct supervision and not yet counted as a working member of a crew

tiers.name: Firefighter
tiers.what_the_role_is: a working member of a crew, expected to hold their position on a task and to communicate what they find

tiers.name: Driver / operator
tiers.what_the_role_is: responsible for getting the apparatus there and for what it can then do; a technical role with its own qualification

tiers.name: Company officer
tiers.what_the_role_is: supervises one company, owns its accountability, and is the first person on most incidents who is making decisions rather than executing them

tiers.name: Chief officer
tiers.what_the_role_is: commands multiple companies or an incident, and is accountable for strategy, risk and the people at it

tiers.name: Prevention, inspection and investigation roles
tiers.what_the_role_is: the side of the service that works before and after the incident: code enforcement, plan review, origin and cause

law.name: Law Enforcement

representation.endorsement_note: no organization named here has reviewed, approved or endorsed any part of this pack, and none has been contacted
kinds: police labour union or benevolent association
public employee union representing civilian and sworn staff
professional association of chiefs and sheriffs
representation.what_they_do_here: representation in this service is split between fraternal bodies, bargaining units and chiefs' associations, which want different things; the pack names the kinds rather than picking one

law.scope: patrol response, investigation, traffic, court process and the scene-security role at almost every other service's incidents

tiers.name: Cadet / academy recruit
tiers.what_the_role_is: in a basic academy, not yet certified, no independent authority to act

tiers.name: Probationary officer in field training
tiers.what_the_role_is: certified but riding with a field training officer; every decision is reviewed

tiers.name: Patrol officer / deputy
tiers.what_the_role_is: working a beat alone or with a partner, making the first decision at most calls

tiers.name: First-line supervisor
tiers.what_the_role_is: supervises a squad, reviews their reports and their force, and is the first accountability layer

tiers.name: Mid-level command
tiers.what_the_role_is: runs a shift, a district or a unit; sets the local priorities and owns the resourcing

tiers.name: Agency executive
tiers.what_the_role_is: chief, sheriff or commissioner: accountable to a governing body and to the public for what the agency does

social.name: Social Work and Crisis Response

representation.endorsement_note: no organization named here has reviewed, approved or endorsed any part of this pack, and none has been contacted
kinds: public employee union representing county and state behavioural health and child welfare staff
service employees union representing non-profit and hospital behavioural health workers
representation.what_they_do_here: the professional association owns the ethical code; the unions bargain the caseload, and caseload is a safety question in this service the way staffing is in the other four

social.scope: behavioural health crisis response, co-response alongside police and EMS, disaster behavioural health, case work and the long tail of a disaster that arrives months later

tiers.name: Peer support specialist
tiers.what_the_role_is: credentialed on the basis of lived experience rather than a degree, and a distinct role rather than a junior clinician

tiers.name: Bachelor-level case worker
tiers.what_the_role_is: carries a caseload, navigates systems, works under supervision

tiers.name: Master-level clinician, pre-licence
tiers.what_the_role_is: clinical work under a licensed supervisor, accumulating the hours the state requires

tiers.name: Licensed clinical social worker
tiers.what_the_role_is: independently licensed, may supervise, carries the clinical accountability

tiers.name: Clinical or programme supervisor
tiers.what_the_role_is: responsible for other people's clinical decisions and for the conditions they make them in

tiers.name: Programme director
tiers.what_the_role_is: owns the service design, the staffing and the relationship with the other four services
